Reward Points Awards And Redemption.role_definition: This service domain handles the allocation and redemption of rewards points for customer transaction activity. In order to determine the reward point transaction and apply associated costs the service domain will access reward point arrangement agreements with the customers, merchants and related rewards programs. Note that the interactions between reward programs can be quite complex when 3rd party reward programs are integrated with the bank's own reward programs
Reward Points Awards And Redemption.example_of_use:
Example of use:
A customer redeems bank reward points in order to finance a purchase with a bank associated vendor for air travel. The financial transaction engages the service domain in order to determine redemption requirements and associated payment requirements
Reward Points Awards And Redemption.executive_summary: Handle the allocation and redemption of rewards points for customer transaction activity
Reward Points Awards And Redemption.key_features:
Financial transaction evaluation (price to agreements)
Reward point redemption transaction
Associated cash payment initiation

Rewards Delivery.role_definition: The Rewards Delivery service domain orchestrates the entire end-to-end  process for delivering a redeemed reward, from ascertaining availability, allocating the reward and  informing the partner, issuing a reward certificate or providing delivery instructions to the partner, and following through until completion of delivery.
Rewards Delivery.example_of_use: The hotel is informed of the hotel room nights awarded to a customer so that the hotel reserves the room and a reward certificate is sent to the customer to be presented at the hotel at the time of check-in.
Rewards Delivery.executive_summary: The service domain orchestrates the entire end-to-end  process for delivering a redeemed reward.
Rewards Delivery.key_features: - Verify availability of requested reward, ascertaining selection preference and request allocation - Inform Rewards Partner of allocation - Determining delivery method - Issue Reward Certificate - Provide delivery instructions to the partner - Update delivery status and recording feedback.

Rewards Inventory.role_definition: The Rewards Inventory service domain maintains the inventory of available and allocated individual rewards and orchestrates their availability, allocation and redemption status. The inventory for a particular reward may need to be managed by specific partitions (e.g., peroids and/or geographic locations).
Rewards Inventory.example_of_use: Presents and allocates from a set of theater tickets requested by the customer for rewards redemption.
Rewards Inventory.executive_summary: The service domain handles the allocation of rewards from available inventory.
Rewards Inventory.key_features: - Configure rewards inventory for different reward categories - Maintain inventory of rewards by specified partitions (e.g., location, date, etc.) - Provide context sensitive list of rewards available for allocation - Allocate reward using specified criteria for each reward type - Enforce specified restrictions (e.g. blackout periods) - Record allocation instance with associated details - Update allocation instance for redemption, expiration, etc.

Rewards Menu.role_definition: The Rewards Menu service domain handles the context sensitive presentation and selection of rewards associated with an Incentive Program, that a customer may redeem. The rewards are grouped into Menus which are associated with one or more Incentive Programs. A comprehensive set of attributes associated with each reward is presented, including a reference to the partners involved in providing and delivering the reward and a reference to the corresponding Rewards Inventory instance.
Rewards Menu.example_of_use: The customer is presented with options available for redemption for the indicated number of points. Of the available options, the customer selects two rewards: one for transfer or points to an Airline frequent flyer account, and the second for a free hotel room on specific dates.
Rewards Menu.executive_summary: The service domain presents a set of eligible rewards a customer can select from.
Rewards Menu.key_features: - Configure Rewards menu attributes for different types of rewards that may be used for either value driven incentives or service driven incentives - Maintain rewards attributes such as redemption eligibility requirements, redemption qualification criteria, and redemption rules. - Reference associated partners and provide partner compensation rate for the reward - Provide points conversion rate for transfers to partner loyalty programs - Provide redemption terms to be displayed to customers - Provide alerts for rewards that are low on inventory or are due to expire - Support ongoing maintenance of rewards comprising a Rewards Menu, including addition, sunsetting, renewal, etc.

Card Clearing.role_definition: The behavior varies depending on the role of the participant bank/network. A card acquiring Bank consolidates all incoming transactions from Merchants, determining their routing, and   transmission to the respective Card Networks. For the Card Networks it receives and consolidates the transactions from all Acquiring Banks and to distributes and routes them to the respective Card Issuing Banks. For the Card Issuing Banks it receives their cardholder transactions from the Card Networks and routes them to the instance of the Credit/Charge Card service domain which is responsible for the card used in the transaction. The transactions may include charges, refunds, and chargebacks.
Card Clearing.example_of_use: An Acquiring Bank receives charge transactions submitted by Merchants through Point of Sale Terminals or batch submission for recurring billing and forwards these transactions to the respective Card Issuing Banks through the Card Network (e.g. Visa, MC, AMEX, Diners, etc.). This process may take place multiple times during the day.
Card Clearing.executive_summary: This service domain orchestrates the capture and consolidation of card financial transactions originating from various sources, such as POS Network, E-Commerce Gateway, ATM Network, or Card Case Management. It also handles the clearing of the transactions from the Acquirers to the Issuers through the Card Networks
Card Clearing.key_features:
Card transaction capture and addressing
FX conversion and fee handling
Interchange fee handling
Transaction matching and reconciliation
Transaction routing

Card Financial Settlement.role_definition:
This service domain is used by the Card Network to initiate either gross or net settlement for the charges cleared during a specified period and to issue settlement instructions to the Issuing and Acquiring Banks. This requires the Card Network to issue settlement instructions to each Issuing Bank directing them to remit the total amounts corresponding to the cleared charges to designated bank accounts that are managed by the Card Network, which in turn makes the corresponding remittances to the designated bank accounts for the Card Issuers.
The service domain is also used by the Issuing and Acquiring banks to perform reconciliation of the settlement instructions against the cleared charges and to initiate remittances through the Payment Order service domain.
Card Financial Settlement.example_of_use: Card Charge transactions that are acquired from the Merchants by the Acquiring Bank and forwarded to the Issuing Banks through Card Clearing are periodically settled (generally once a day).
Card Financial Settlement.executive_summary: This service domain orchestrates the settlement of the transactions between the Issuers and the Acquirers through the Card Networks.
Card Financial Settlement.key_features:
Customer case capture and classification.
Case related information consolidation.
Customer case diagnosis and decisioning.
Card Case Initiation.
Customer case resolution implementation.

Card eCommerce Gateway.role_definition: This service domain is used by the Card Acquiring bank to handle the authentication, authorization and submission of a Card payment from an e-commerce merchant. It supports the "3-D" Secure method of authentication which routes the authentication request to the Card Issuing Bank, which may use multi-factor authentication for the authentication of the Card and the Cardholder. It also handles the routing of the authorization request through the Card Transaction Switch service domain and the routing of the submitted charges to the Card Clearing service domain.
Card eCommerce Gateway.example_of_use:
Example of use:
When a Card is used for making a payment on an e-commerce site of a Merchant, the Merchant initiates three steps to process the payment: 1) request authentication of the Card and the Cardholder, 2) request an authorization of the charge amount, and 3) submit the charge details to the Card Acquirer for processing and payment.
Card eCommerce Gateway.executive_summary: This service domain orchestrates the processing of e-commerce transactions for authentication, authorization and capture of the financial transactions.
Card eCommerce Gateway.key_features:
e-Commerce transaction capture
Card holder authentication
Transaction authorization
e-Commerce transaction batch submission handling

Central Cash Handling.role_definition: This service domain is responsible for tracking the available cash inventory held centrally and distributed/collected throughout the branch/ATM network and making allocation/redistribution requests to ensure adequate float is available at all locations and that excess cash at any location is transferred to central secure locations as appropriate. Also coordinating with other banks and central banks to ensure sufficient cash is on hand to support the branch network requirements
Central Cash Handling.example_of_use:
Example of use:
The central cash management function reviews the current and projected available float at locations across the network to ensure adequate supply to meet projected demand
Central Cash Handling.executive_summary: Track cash inventory, project demand and allocate inventory across the branch/ATM network
Central Cash Handling.key_features:
Cash inventory usage and availability tracking
Cash inventory requirements evaluation and planning
Cash float availability and allocation oversight

Cheque Processing.role_definition: This service domains handles the processing of paper checks, performing the necessary checks and extracting the transaction details required to create a payment transaction record stream. This includes MICR number processing and character recognition facilities
Cheque Processing.example_of_use:
Example of use:
A batch of paper cheques captured at a merchant location is processed to initiate settlement processing
Cheque Processing.executive_summary: Handle the processing of paper cheques, generating financial transactions for processing
Cheque Processing.key_features:
Paper cheque scanning and content verification
Cancelled cheque identification
Financial transaction generation

Financial Gateway.role_definition: This service domain supports the operational connections with the range of financial networks that support interbank and financial institution connectivity. This includes SWIFT, ACH gateways, and market exchange/regulatory reporting connections. The service domain does not create content itself, it provides a real-time, near real-time or batch message exchange service between (financial) institutions for various units within the bank. It may maintain and apply authentication and encryption keys to the transmitted messages and validate message structure, as necessary. It also provides operational message recovery and retransmission facilities as appropriate.
Financial Gateway.example_of_use: During the 24 hour cycle, the bank's 'wire room' unit establishes the connections with the different payments, SWIFT and reporting networks
Financial Gateway.executive_summary: This service domain operates automated message interfaces to secure networks such as SWIFT, TELEX, ACH and Financial Market/Exchange reporting services
Financial Gateway.key_features:
Operate the bank's connection to financial networks
Handle inbound and outbound financial messages
Maintain and apply encryption/authentication keys
Handle service configuration and operational controls

Financial Message Analysis.role_definition: Track and analyze financial message traffic to identify anomalies and potential fraudulent activity
Financial Message Analysis.example_of_use: A pattern of financial message traffic for a major counterparty is analyzed to reveal possible fraudulent behaviors

Payment Confirmation.role_definition: This service domain performs the required checks that include  internal bank policies and account eligibility checks, ensuring funds availability, verifying any customer, payment rail or counterparty preferences, performing limits checks both for bank/customer/product limits as well as any counterpary specific limits,  earmarking of funds in both customer's funding account and the counterparty related holding account.
Payment Confirmation.example_of_use: A customer payment order once authorized by the customer is passed to the bank's back office where various internal bank checks including an AML review are made before settlement
Payment Confirmation.executive_summary: This service domain performs the required internal bank and regulatory checks, optionally earmarking funds, before clearing a payment transaction for settlement
Payment Confirmation.key_features:
Pricing/FX Processing
Limits check
Risk Checks (AML, Credit, Fraud, Operational)
Flexible funding source
Account Status/Eligibility
Funds authorization (based on funds availability and risk assessment)
Earmarking of funds

Payment Orchestration.example_of_use: A customer initiates a funds transfer request indicating the account for the source of funds and the beneficiary bank and account details, which are used by the bank to determine the appropriate payment rail and for routing and confirming the successful completion of the transfer.
Payment Orchestration.executive_summary: This service domains processes the movement of funds between accounts within the bank or to/from an account held with another bank, coordinating the required risk checks, selecting the appropriate payment mechanism, and ensuring completion of the transaction.
Payment Orchestration.key_features:
Determine the appropriate payment mechanism
Perform bank and regulatory checks on the payee and payer
Retrieve counterparty payment instructions/preferences
Generate creditor and debtor instructions
Structure payment execution requests to match preferences
Oversee counterparty netting arrangements
Confirm (and report) both legs of the movement are completed
Initiate Payment Order for approved Request to Pay transactions

Payment Rail.role_definition:
This Service Domain handles the operational interface with one or more external payment services or 'payment rails'. This includes formatting outbound messages, ensuring compliance with rules and standards defined by external payment services, adherance to defined payment service schedules, supporting store and forward of payments for clearing and settlement purposes, and extracting and mapping inbound message content for internal processing during the scheduled operating sessions of the payment service.This Service Domain will interact with a paired Holding Account Service Domain to handle the underlying recording and movement of funds between the bank and service provider.
The Service Domain also handles reconciliation and settlement with Payment Schemes and Counterparties. While this is particularly relevant for schemes that use deferred and batched processing, it could also be used for end of day reconciliation and settlement of fees/charges for real-time payment schemes.
Payment Rail.example_of_use: The bank receives a payment notification for one of its customers from the payment service. Once lower level message security checks have been performed the interpreted message is passed to the Payment Order Instruction Service Domains for further processing.
Payment Rail.executive_summary: This Service Domain handles the operational interface with payment service providers, formatting outbound transactions and onward routing inbound transactions during scheduled operating sessions. It also links to holding account facilities for net payment handling
Payment Rail.key_features: Handle outbound payment transactions Handle inbound payment transactions Handle transaction warehousing (delayed send) Handle transaction update, repair Handle holding account access and reconciliation Handle scheme and counterparty liquidity risk management Handle interbank or scheme fees and charges Handle interbank settlement through Payment Authority Handle service configuration and operational controls

Payment Settlement.role_definition: This service domain performs the funds movements between the customer account and an internal bank account or holding account to ensure funds are available for interbank settlement by the Payment Rail. This may involve the principal payment transfer as well as for fees.
Payment Settlement.example_of_use: A payment once authorized and confirmed is passed for settlement where one or more funds transfers are intiated through an external payment rail
Payment Settlement.executive_summary: This service domain performs the funds movements between customer and internal bank accounts in support of internal and interbank settlement using any appropriate payment rail
Payment Settlement.key_features:
Funds movement between Funding Account and Holding Account
Reversing Earmarked funds

Card Authorization.role_definition: The proposed card transaction is requested by a merchant and routed through the Acquirer and Card Network to the Issuer. The authorization decision is automated and can be extremely complex. Transactions may be passed for manual checks by on-line service representatives for out of pattern purchases. Note that authorized transaction amounts may vary from the actual final amount (e.g. pre authorized hotel/car hire and charged meals excluding tips) and in cases there will be no financial transaction for an authorized transaction if the customer chooses to pay using a different card/cash. While this function is primarily performed by the Issuer, Acquirers and Card Networks may perform Stand-in Authorization and forward the results to the Issuer for recording.
Card Authorization.example_of_use: A credit card customer makes a large purchase, the card authorization triggers a verbal check of the customer details for security and the authorization is given
Card Authorization.executive_summary: This service domain is responsible for the real time card authorization decisions for credit/charge cards.
Card Authorization.key_features:
Card device verification checks
Card member identity verification
Credit checks
Fraud detection checks

Card Network Participant Facility.role_definition: Cards issued by banks are affiliated with one of many international Card Networks, such as Visa, Master Card, Diners, American Express. This service domain is used by the Card Network for setting up Acquiring and Issuing Bank accounts and their terms and conditions.
Card Network Participant Facility.example_of_use: The Card Network signs up Acquiring Banks for recruiting and setting up accounts for merchants and Issuing Banks for issuing cards to its customers.
Card Network Participant Facility.executive_summary: This service domain orchestrates the activities related to the inclusion of new Acquirers and Issuers in the Card Network, their terms and conditions and their status.
Card Network Participant Facility.key_features:
Acquiring bank facility terms administration
Issuing bank facility terms administration
Participant bank service status maintenance

Card Transaction Capture.role_definition: Capture and consolidate the cardcharges and refunds received from merchant/point of sale or subscription type charges received from Merchants through Card Terminal Operation. It also consolidates Chargebacks received through Card Case, and financial adjustments resulting from customer claims, processed through Customer Case.This SD has a role within the Acquiring bank in consolidating and enriching the transactions throug additional information received from merchant systems such as Airline reservation systems and separting the payables transactions for processing through the Merchant Acquiring facility and sumbitting the enriched charge transactions for clearing through the Card Netwrok. Similarly, the SD has a role withing the Issuing bank in consolidating the transactions and distributing them to the relevant financial facility for posting.
Card Transaction Capture.example_of_use:
Example of use:
A card user uses their card to pay for a meal at a restaurant
Card Transaction Capture.executive_summary: A distributed facility to capture card transactions at the point of sale
Card Transaction Capture.key_features:
Transaction capture.
Transaction consolidation from multiple sources.Transaction enrichment from information sources from third paries.
Holding and releasing future dated transactions.
Transaction batch reporting for clearing through the network.
Delivering transaction streams for posting to financial facility.

Card Transaction Tracking.role_definition: Card Transaction Tracking Service Domain holds the transaction details for the complete life-cycle. This includes pre-authorization, authorization, top-up authorization, financial charge, tips and additional charges and charge-back related. This transaction log is written to by Card Authorization, Card Transaction Capture and Card Clearing  with separate instances being maintained by the Acquirer, Card Network and Card Issuer.
Card Transaction Tracking.example_of_use: The transaction events for a customer using their card to book and eventually pay their hotel bill are recorded in the log
Card Transaction Tracking.executive_summary: Maintain a log of credit card bookings and authorizations for operational and management information, tracking and reconciliation purposes.
Card Transaction Tracking.key_features:
Capture and track transaction updates from authorization activity.
Capture and track transaction updates from Card Transaction Capture for charges, refunds and reversals.
Capture and track updates from Card Clearingfor chargebacks related activity.

Corporate Card Service.role_definition: The Corporte Card Service service domain orchestrates the fulfillment of all service obligations for Corporate customers in relation to different types of Croporate Card products, such as, Corporate T&E Card, Business Travel Accounts, and Purchase Card. This service domain maintains Corporate Card Master Accounts representing Corporate entity and its organizational structure hierarchy under which the individual employee cards accounts are controlled, while the services for individual card accounts is fulfilled by the "Credit Card" service domain.
Corporate Card Service.example_of_use: A large corporation enters a multi-national agreement with the Bank for the issuance of Corporate Cards to its executives, requiring customized design of services and reporting to be provided at the different levels of the Corporate hierarchy.
Corporate Card Service.executive_summary: The Service Domain orchestrates the fulfillment servicing for corporate level card arrangements, managing any master accounts and the organizational/divisional set-up, controlling and coordinating the interactions with underlying employess card accounts
Corporate Card Service.key_features:
- Maintain Corporate Card Master Accounts representing Corporate entity which has contracted for any of the following types of Corporate Card products:
a) Corporate T&E Card issued to employees
b) Business Travel Account used for travel expenses by employees who are not eligible for Corporate T&E Card
c) Purchase Card used by designated employees for making purchase of supplies, raw materials, etc.
- Link the Corporate Card Master Accounts to represent Corporate hierachy, e.g.: Department - Division - Regional HQ - Country HQ - Global HQ
- Identify and record Corporate Card Terms and Conditions at each level of corporate hierarchy, with the ability to override terms inherited from superior levels
- Allow for Central Billing accounts for certain types of charges, e.g., Airline Charges, Fees, etc.
